HSIC.thesis_one_line: The largest US dental/medical distributor, raising guidance twice this year on a self-funded cost program, but carrying more debt than it looks at first glance.
kill_criteria: Consolidated net debt/EBITDA (total debt incl. short-term borrowings ÷ TTM EBITDA) rises above 4.0x without a specific, disclosed deleveraging plan.
FY2026 guidance (non-GAAP EPS $5.29–$5.39, sales growth 4.5–5.5%, given 2026-08-04) is cut at the Q3 2026 or Q4 2026 release.
Consolidated gross margin falls below 30.5% for two consecutive quarters (versus the ~31–32% range held since 2024).
The value-creation program's disclosed run-rate savings fall short of the $125M by year-end 2026 target by more than 20% when next reported.
A new, material legal proceeding (antitrust, regulatory, or a fresh cyber incident) is disclosed in a subsequent 10-Q/10-K Legal Proceedings note.
key_adverse_facts: Consolidated total debt (long-term debt/capital leases $2,438M plus short-term borrowings $1,024M at 2026-06-27) is materially larger than long-term debt alone; net debt/EBITDA ≈ 3.3x, matching the triage's own 3.4x figure -- confirmed, not overturned.
Short-term borrowings roughly doubled from $913M (Q3 2025) to over $1.0bn (Q1–Q2 2026), coinciding with continued open-market and accelerated share buybacks.
GAAP vs. non-GAAP gap is wide (FY2025 GAAP EPS $3.27 vs. non-GAAP $4.97, a 34% gap), driven mainly by acquisition intangible amortization and restructuring costs.
CEO Frederick M. Lowery has been in the role only since 2026-03-02 (succeeding Stanley M. Bergman after 35 years), so the value-creation program's execution has only two quarters of track record.
Q1 2026 operating cash flow was negative (-$97M, quarter-alone), a working-capital swing that reversed in Q2 2026 ($242M) -- not a trend, but a data point worth watching.
data_conflicts: The triage flagged the legacy Dental Supply Antitrust Litigation and the 2023 ransomware/cyber incident as open red flags to close out; this dossier finds neither is disclosed as a pending/material matter in the FY2025 10-K's Note 17 (Commitments and Contingencies) -- only an immaterial opioid-supply-chain MDL (<0.4% of sales) is disclosed, and the cyber incident's insurance-recovery process itself concluded in Q1 2025. This dossier treats both triage-flagged items as closed, a confirmation/resolution rather than a conflict.

b1_live_scores.csv shows only a middling leverage percentile (pct_leverage 0.395) for HSIC; this dossier's own build of total debt (including short-term borrowings, which the model's leverage factor may not fully capture) puts net debt/EBITDA at ~3.3x, elevated for the sector -- worth flagging as a possible gap between the model's leverage read and the fuller balance-sheet picture.

confidence_in_thesis.reason: the guidance-raise track record and the closed status of the triage's two named litigation/cyber red flags are strong and primary-source-verified, but the ~3.3x leverage (funded partly by fast-growing short-term borrowings) and the new CEO's short track record are genuine, unresolved sources of uncertainty this pass could not close out

scenario_returns_3y.scenario_basis: Starting point: $86.37 close, FY2025 non-GAAP diluted EPS $4.97, FY2026 guided non-GAAP EPS $5.29-$5.39 (midpoint $5.34), NTM non-GAAP P/E ~16.2x, no dividend. Bear: the value-creation program stalls, distributor margin pressure returns, leverage rises further; multiple compresses toward 13-14x on flat-to-low-single-digit adjusted EPS growth. Base: guidance is delivered, adjusted EPS grows at a high-single-digit pace (~8%/yr) as the $200M+ cost program layers in atop mid-single-digit organic growth; multiple re-rates modestly toward the historical ~17-18x range. Bull: cost-program savings exceed the disclosed target and organic growth accelerates further, adjusted EPS grows low-double-digit, multiple re-rates to the historical ~20x high. All annualised over 3 years; no dividend to add.

HSY.thesis_one_line: One of America's two big chocolate makers, recovering fast from a cocoa-cost shock, but much of 2026's growth is a snapback off a low base.
kill_criteria: FY2026 guidance (adjusted EPS growth 32.5-35%, net sales growth 4.5-5%, given 2026-07-30) is cut at the Q3 2026 release.
Cocoa or other key commodity costs re-accelerate materially, evidenced by adjusted gross margin declining for two consecutive quarters from the H1 2026 level.
Net debt/EBITDA (consolidated) rises above 2.5x without a specific, disclosed acquisition or buyback rationale.
The common-stock dividend ($1.370/quarter, $5.480/yr) is cut or suspended.
Organic constant-currency net sales growth falls below 2% for two consecutive quarters (versus the 3-3.5% FY2026 guided floor).
key_adverse_facts: The FY2025 collapse (GAAP EPS -60.3%, adjusted EPS -32.7%, operating profit -50.3%) was driven by record cocoa costs; the entire FY2026 recovery narrative (guided adjusted EPS growth of 32.5-35%) is substantially a snapback off that artificially depressed base, not yet proven as a durable multi-year re-rate.

Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow (~$2,228M) is running above both FY2024 ($1,926M) and FY2025 ($1,823M) actuals -- this dossier treats it as likely inflated by a temporary working-capital/cocoa-cost-timing tailwind and uses a normalized ~$1,874M base for valuation instead.

Consolidated total debt has grown to ~$5,611M (net debt ~$4,820M, net debt/EBITDA ~1.8x), up from a materially lower base in 2024, funding continued buybacks, a flat (not grown) dividend through the crisis year, and the 2025 LesserEvil acquisition.
Cocoa is a volatile, weather- and geopolitically-sensitive commodity; a renewed price spike would directly reverse the current margin-recovery tailwind that the whole 2026 thesis depends on.
Q2 2026's GAAP EPS ($2.26) exceeded adjusted EPS ($1.90) -- an inverted gap this dossier did not fully decompose this pass, flagged as an open item.
data_conflicts: None identified between b1 quant data and filings; the model's moderate composite (0.488, decile 5) and weak momentum score (fam_M 0.184) are consistent with this dossier's own read that the market has not yet fully re-rated the stock for the confirmed 2026 recovery.

confidence_in_thesis.reason: the guidance-raise track record and the FCF resilience through the FY2025 shock are strong and primary-source-verified, but the durability of the 32-35% adjusted-EPS-growth guide beyond 2026 (once the depressed base normalizes) is unproven, and cocoa-cost volatility is a structural, unhedgeable-in-full risk to the whole thesis

scenario_returns_3y.scenario_basis: Starting point: $166.37 close, FY2025 adjusted EPS $6.31, FY2026 guided adjusted EPS $8.20-$8.52 (midpoint $8.36), NTM adjusted P/E ~19.9x, dividend $5.480/yr (~3.3% yield, held flat through FY2025). Bear: cocoa costs spike again or organic growth disappoints, adjusted EPS growth reverts to low-single-digit off this higher base, multiple compresses toward 16x (the trough seen during the cocoa crisis). Base: EPS growth normalizes to mid-to-high single digit (~7%/yr) after the 2026 snapback, multiple holds near 20x, dividend continues at ~3.3% yield. Bull: cocoa costs stay favorable and innovation/pricing sustain double-digit-plus EPS growth, multiple re-rates toward Hershey's historical 22-25x premium. All annualised over 3 years, dividends added undiscounted.

LII.thesis_one_line: A best-in-class HVAC compounder, cheap versus peers, but the July 2026 guidance cut shows its growth is turning more acquisition-driven and less organic.
kill_criteria: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance ($23.00-$24.00, given 2026-07-29) is cut again at the Q3 2026 or Q4 2026 release.
Home Comfort Solutions revenue does not show sequential stabilization (i.e., a second consecutive quarter of YoY decline worse than -7%) by Q1 2027.
Consolidated net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.5x as commercial paper continues to fund acquisitions, without a disclosed deleveraging plan.
Building Climate Solutions organic growth decelerates below 8% for two consecutive quarters (versus the 15-26% pace of the last two quarters).
Free cash flow for FY2026 comes in below the low end of the company's own guided $750M-$850M range.
key_adverse_facts: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance was cut at the Q2 2026 release (to $23.00-$24.00 from $23.50-$25.00, top end down 4%) even as revenue guidance was simultaneously raised (to ~8% growth from 6-7%, driven by a bigger acquisition contribution) -- the incremental growth on offer is increasingly acquisition-funded and margin-diluting, not pure organic operating leverage. The triage's own red-flag list did not capture this cut.

Home Comfort Solutions, still the larger segment (~61% of Q2 2026 revenue), fell 7% YoY in Q2 2026 and 10% in Q1 2026, with new-construction-driven softness management itself calls a 'meaningful headwind'.

Commercial paper (the funding source for a string of recent bolt-on acquisitions -- Duro Dyne, Supco, Comfort-Aire, Century, Heat Controller) rose 82% in six months, from $226.0M (2025-12-31) to $412.0M (2026-06-30).

The company runs on a very thin equity base (~$1.3bn stockholders' equity against a ~$13bn market cap) -- the headline ~72% ROE the model reads is in large part a capital-structure artefact of aggressive historical buybacks, not solely an operating-margin phenomenon; the model's own Quality family score (0.117) is well below what the ROE alone would suggest and this dossier does not overturn that lower read.

The company changed its inventory accounting method from LIFO to FIFO effective Q4 2025; all 2025 comparatives in company releases (and this dossier) are on the restated FIFO basis, which should be kept in mind for any YoY comparison to pre-2025 figures.
data_conflicts: The triage flagged 'R454B refrigerant transition cost/complexity' as a red flag; this dossier finds the FY2025 10-K states the transition to GWP<=700 refrigerants 'became effective January 1, 2025', i.e., it is a completed, already-lapped transition being reported on, not a forward risk -- a correction versus the triage's forward-looking framing.

b1_live_scores.csv shows a very high pct_roe (0.94) but a low overall Quality family score (fam_Q 0.117, dragged down by pct_leverage 0.30 and pct_asset_growth 0.14); this dossier confirms the model's lower Quality read is the more calibrated one given the thin equity base and the rising commercial-paper-funded leverage, rather than treating the headline ROE as straightforwardly bullish.

confidence_in_thesis.reason: Building Climate Solutions' growth and margin trajectory are strong and primary-source-verified, and the R454B risk the triage flagged is confirmed resolved, but the July 2026 guidance cut and the rising commercial-paper-funded leverage for M&A are genuine, unresolved sources of uncertainty this pass could not close out

scenario_returns_3y.scenario_basis: Starting point: $373.77 close, FY2025 GAAP diluted EPS $22.79 (FIFO-restated), FY2026 guided adjusted EPS $23.00-$24.00 (midpoint $23.50), NTM P/E ~15.9x, dividend ~$5.20/yr estimated (~1.4% yield).
